issues.title: Persistent USE keyspace failures can drain a reachable node's pool to Broken
issues.verdictReason: handle_ready_connection's new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm (connection_pool.rs:900-910) always drops the connection and, once is_filling() is false and is_empty() is true, calls update_shared_conns which sets shared_conns to Broken and (via emit_events) fires a Lost event; base code logged a warn! and still pushed the connection into the pool regardless of USE outcome, so a persistently failing USE never emptied the pool.
issues.scopeReason: The new discard-on-keyspace-failure behavior is exactly what this PR adds.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: A USE that keeps failing causes every new connection to be dropped and the pool to drain to Broken(UseKeyspaceError), firing a Lost event for a still-reachable node, whereas the base only warned and kept the connection.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: A USE that keeps failing causes every new connection to be dropped and the pool to drain to Broken(UseKeyspaceError), firing a Lost event for a still-reachable node, whereas the base only warned and kept the connection.

issues.scopeReason: The log level change is part of this PR's diff.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: The failure log level was lowered from warn! to debug!, and the error only reaches last_error when the pool is not filling and is empty, so repeated keyspace failures are invisible at default log levels while the pool isn't empty.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: The failure log level was lowered from warn! to debug!, and the error only reaches last_error when the pool is not filling and is empty, so repeated keyspace failures are invisible at default log levels while the pool isn't empty.
